A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoPRS work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoPRS benchmark results, training and inference correlations, ablations, and qualitative segmentation results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original CoPRS results and adds CoT consistency analysis, backbone experiments, convergence measurements, and inference-cost comparisons.

M1.justification: The concentration token, attention-derived positional prior, decoder, joint GRPO/segmentation objective, and inference procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 explains the existing heatmap computation, and alternative backbones are evaluated as ablations without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on the RefCOCO series and evaluate zero-shot reasoning segmentation on ReasonSeg. The added diagnostics use these existing datasets and task requirements; no new domain or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparators within each benchmark. The new efficiency comparisons reuse Seg-R1 and Seg-Zero, while the backbone studies compare CoPRS variants. Correcting the SegLLM citation does not introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gemini-2.5-Flash scoring of 1,901 RefCOCO+ testA examples, LLaVA-1.5 and SAM backbone controls, and parameter/GFLOP evaluation. The group-size study changes from G=2/4/8 across three datasets to G=2/4/8/16 across RefCOCO+ splits, adding a convergence criterion of less than 10% loss fluctuation over 300 steps. The main benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 add direct CoT-quality versus segmentation analysis, MLLM and vision-backbone ablations, and convergence-efficiency analysis; Appendix B.4 adds inference-cost analysis. These substantially broaden the questions tested. Training-mode, reward, and loss studies are retained in revised displays, while Appendix C's success and failure cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use OLS regression and mean-confidence bands, with the same stated scaling procedure. The additional correlations extend this practice without introducing new uncertainty estimation. Neither version reports repeated-seed benchmark summaries or significance tests; CoT sample counts and convergence counts are not repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New results include CoT correlations of 0.65 with heatmap IoU and 0.44 with mask IoU, backbone comparisons, and computational costs. Retained ablation values also change: RefCOCOg's combined-training result is 67.2 in v1 Table 3 but approximately 76 in v2 Figure 6b. The PDFs do not explain whether these revisions reflect corrections or changed conditions.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a mathematical specification for the new CoT consistency score: a weighted average of four criteria with weights 0.3/0.2/0.3/0.2. This is a limited added metric definition. The method equations and Appendix A's PPO/GRPO derivations remain substantively unchanged; Algorithm 1 restates the existing attention computation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the empirical alignment claim from heatmap–mask correspondence to correspondence among CoT quality, heatmaps, and masks. The central positional-prior contribution, unified training framework, and benchmark-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning backbone portability, the efficiency tradeoff favoring G=8, and format reward as a regularizer. It also interprets the new CoT correlations as better reasoning leading to better segmentation, exceeding what association alone establishes. Tiny-object and crowded-instance limitations were already discussed in v1 Appendix C.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.2 specifies the five format-reward cases, the 2,048-character penalty threshold, last-token reward assignment, and heatmap pseudocode. Existing training configurations are retained. The abstract replaces a repository link and an asserted release with a future-release promise; both versions also promise release upon acceptance elsewhere.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Gemini 2.5 report and Yin et al.'s process-reward modeling work to support the automatic evaluator, and corrects SegLLM attribution in the experimental setup. The broader positioning against latent and textual-coordinate reasoning methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 contains sentence-level polishing, acronym clarification, and local reorganization of the correlation and ablation discussions. Appendix B gains design-details and efficiency subsections. The overall section sequence and most existing methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reworked: four numerical ablation tables become four-panel Figure 6, and v2 adds a CoT correlation figure, consistency table, backbone tables, efficiency tables, and Algorithm 1. Existing diagrams and qualitative panels are retained or renumbered. The replacement ablation plots have crowded labels and omit printed exact values.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's heatmap–mask analysis, v2 directly examines CoT alignment and adds useful backbone and computational-cost controls. Explicit reward-case documentation also improves reproducibility. These gains are limited by causal wording unsupported by the correlational design, unexplained ablation-value revisions, less readable replacement plots, and removal of the repository link in favor of a future-release statement.
